/-!
# Decidability of the theory of $\mathbb{F}_p((t))$

Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems in mathematics asks whether the first-order theory of the
field of formal Laurent series over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ is decidable. Here $\mathbb{Z}_p$ is the prime
field $\mathbb{F}_p = \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$: Laurent series over the $p$-adic integers do not
form a field.

The theory of a field $K$ is its complete theory $\mathrm{Th}(K)$ in the first-order language of
rings $\{+, \cdot, -, 0, 1\}$, that is, the set of all sentences true in $K$. It is *decidable* if
there is an algorithm which, given a sentence, decides whether it lies in $\mathrm{Th}(K)$.
Mathlib has no computability structure on first-order sentences, so this file fixes a Gödel
numbering of sentences (`Decidable.godelNumber`, built from
`FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormula.listEncode`) and defines a theory to be decidable
(`Decidable.IsDecidableTheory`) if some computable function `ℕ → Bool` decides membership on
Gödel numbers.

The existential theory of $\mathbb{F}_p((t))$ in the language of rings is decidable
(Anscombe–Fehm), but the decidability of the full first-order theory is open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Decidability (logic)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decidability_%28logic%29)
- [S. Anscombe, A. Fehm, *The existential theory of equicharacteristic henselian valued fields*,
  Algebra & Number Theory 10 (2016), 665–683](https://doi.org/10.2140/ant.2016.10.665)
-/

def ringFunctionsEquivFin : (Σ i, Language.ring.Functions i) ≃ Fin 5 where
  toFun
    | ⟨_, .add⟩ => 0
    | ⟨_, .mul⟩ => 1
    | ⟨_, .neg⟩ => 2
    | ⟨_, .zero⟩ => 3
    | ⟨_, .one⟩ => 4
  invFun := ![⟨2, .add⟩, ⟨2, .mul⟩, ⟨1, .neg⟩, ⟨0, .zero⟩, ⟨0, .one⟩]
  left_inv := by rintro ⟨_, f⟩; cases f <;> rfl
  right_inv := by decide

blocks.text:
/-- The five function symbols `+`, `*`, `-`, `0`, `1` of the language of rings, enumerated by
`Fin 5`. -/
def ringFunctionsEquivFin : (Σ i, Language.ring.Functions i) ≃ Fin 5 where
  toFun
    | ⟨_, .add⟩ => 0
    | ⟨_, .mul⟩ => 1
    | ⟨_, .neg⟩ => 2
    | ⟨_, .zero⟩ => 3
    | ⟨_, .one⟩ => 4
  invFun := ![⟨2, .add⟩, ⟨2, .mul⟩, ⟨1, .neg⟩, ⟨0, .zero⟩, ⟨0, .one⟩]
  left_inv := by rintro ⟨_, f⟩; cases f <;> rfl
  right_inv := by decide

def IsDecidableTheory (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : ℕ → Bool, Computable f ∧ ∀ φ : L.Sentence, f (godelNumber φ) = true ↔ φ ∈ T
blocks.docstring:
An `L`-theory `T` (a set of `L`-sentences) is *decidable* if there is a computable function
`f : ℕ → Bool` which, applied to the Gödel number of any sentence `φ`, returns `true` if and
only if `φ ∈ T`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `ComputablePred` (requires a `Primcodable` instance on sentences, which does not exist); `FirstOrder.Language.Theory.IsComplete`/`IsSatisfiable` (different notions).
justification.name: Decidable.IsDecidableTheory
justification.why_needed: The notion of a decidable first-order theory (a computable `ℕ → Bool` deciding membership via Gödel numbers) is absent from Mathlib and the repository.

blocks.name: IsDecidableTheory
blocks.text:
/-- An `L`-theory `T` (a set of `L`-sentences) is *decidable* if there is a computable function
`f : ℕ → Bool` which, applied to the Gödel number of any sentence `φ`, returns `true` if and
only if `φ ∈ T`. -/
def IsDecidableTheory (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : ℕ → Bool, Computable f ∧ ∀ φ : L.Sentence, f (godelNumber φ) = true ↔ φ ∈ T

theorem godelNumber_injective : Function.Injective (godelNumber (L := L)) := by
  intro φ ψ h

    (⟨0, φ⟩ : Σ n, L.BoundedFormula Empty n).2.listEncode =

  simpa using this

claims.decomposer_note: Here $\mathbb{Z}_p$ must be read as the prime field $\mathbb{F}_p=\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ (Laurent series over the p-adic integers do not form a field); the question is whether the complete first-order theory $\mathrm{Th}(\mathbb{F}_p((t)))$ in the language of rings is a computable set of sentences, with the prime $p$ an implicit parameter (so the formalization should fix an arbitrary prime $p$ or quantify over all primes, since the answer could a priori depend on $p$); the existential fragment is known decidable (Anscombe–Fehm 2016) but the full theory is open.
claims.reviewer_why: Final file uses c05's Mathlib-based formulation (Language.ring, completeTheory, compatibleRingOfRing, Gödel numbering via BoundedFormula.listEncode and an explicit computable Encodable instance on the five ring function symbols, IsDecidableTheory := ∃ computable f : ℕ → Bool deciding membership on Gödel numbers), with edits: the symbol encoding is a def made a local instance (avoids a global instance that could later clash with Mathlib), `∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime →` instead of `∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]`, docstrings tightened. Verified: the numbering is Lean-computable (#eval works), injective (proved), the ring-language structure on LaurentSeries (ZMod p) is compatibleRingOfRing (checked with pp.explicit), builds with `lake --wfail build`. c01/c03/c04 are equivalent in content; c02/c06/c08 re-implement syntax/coding by hand (correct but bespoke and less reviewable); c07 is unfaithful: `∃ coding : Primcodable Sentence, ComputablePred ...` is satisfiable for every infinite/coinfinite theory by choosing a non-effective bijective coding, so its statement is trivially answer(True).

claims.decomposer_note: The polynomial ring $\mathbb{C}[t]$ is not a field and its existential theory is already undecidable (Denef 1978), so the intended object is the field of rational functions $\mathbb{C}(t)$ (its field of fractions), for which even Hilbert's tenth problem is open (Poonen, Kollár); the Prop is that $\mathrm{Th}(\mathbb{C}(t))$ in the language of rings (no constants for elements of $\mathbb{C}$, sidestepping uncountability) is decidable, i.e. a computable set of sentences.
claims.reviewer_why: Omitted. Every candidate states `answer(sorry) ↔ IsDecidable(Th(RatFunc ℂ))` with `research open`. To my knowledge (and independently flagged by c01), the full first-order theory of ℂ(t) — indeed of any function field of one variable over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 — was proved undecidable by J.-L. Duret, 'Sur la théorie élémentaire des corps de fonctions', J. Symbolic Logic 51 (1986) 948–956 (cited as such in the Pheidas–Zahidi and Koenigsmann surveys); only Hilbert's tenth problem (existential theory) for ℂ(t) is open (Kollár, Poonen — the only ℂ(t) statement in the cited Poonen sampler). Shipping the full-theory question as `research open` would misclassify a solved problem; I could not verify the citation offline well enough to ship `research solved` with `answer(False)`, and reinterpreting 'theory' as 'existential theory' would not be faithful to the text or the table. So no faithful version could be stated.

context: In logic, a true/false decision problem is decidable if there exists an effective method for deriving the correct answer. Logical systems are decidable if membership in their set of logically valid formulas (or theorems) can be effectively determined. Zeroth-order logic (propositional logic) is decidable, whereas first-order and higher-order logic are not. A theory (set of sentences closed under logical consequence) in a fixed logical system is decidable if there is an effective method for determining whether arbitrary formulas are included in the theory. Many important problems are undecidable, that is, it has been proven that no effective method for determining membership (returning a correct answer after finite, though possibly very long, time in all cases) can exist for them.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The table's readings (𝔽_p((t)) rather than ℤ_p((t)), and ℂ(t) rather than ℂ[t], both in the pure language of rings) are the standard ones and are confirmed by the cited Poonen survey (open status of Hilbert's tenth problem for ℂ(t)).

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Decidability of the theory of $\mathbb{F}_p((t))$

Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems in mathematics asks whether the first-order theory of the
field of formal Laurent series over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ is decidable. Here $\mathbb{Z}_p$ is the prime
field $\mathbb{F}_p = \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$: Laurent series over the $p$-adic integers do not
form a field.

The theory of a field $K$ is its complete theory $\mathrm{Th}(K)$ in the first-order language of
rings $\{+, \cdot, -, 0, 1\}$, that is, the set of all sentences true in $K$. It is *decidable* if
there is an algorithm which, given a sentence, decides whether it lies in $\mathrm{Th}(K)$.
Mathlib has no computability structure on first-order sentences, so this file fixes a Gödel
numbering of sentences (`Decidable.godelNumber`, built from
`FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormula.listEncode`) and defines a theory to be decidable
(`Decidable.IsDecidableTheory`) if some computable function `ℕ → Bool` decides membership on
Gödel numbers.

The existential theory of $\mathbb{F}_p((t))$ in the language of rings is decidable
(Anscombe–Fehm), but the decidability of the full first-order theory is open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Decidability (logic)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decidability_%28logic%29)
- [S. Anscombe, A. Fehm, *The existential theory of equicharacteristic henselian valued fields*,
  Algebra & Number Theory 10 (2016), 665–683](https://doi.org/10.2140/ant.2016.10.665)
-/

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

namespace Decidable

/-- The five function symbols `+`, `*`, `-`, `0`, `1` of the language of rings, enumerated by
`Fin 5`. -/
def ringFunctionsEquivFin : (Σ i, Language.ring.Functions i) ≃ Fin 5 where
  toFun
    | ⟨_, .add⟩ => 0
    | ⟨_, .mul⟩ => 1
    | ⟨_, .neg⟩ => 2
    | ⟨_, .zero⟩ => 3
    | ⟨_, .one⟩ => 4
  invFun := ![⟨2, .add⟩, ⟨2, .mul⟩, ⟨1, .neg⟩, ⟨0, .zero⟩, ⟨0, .one⟩]
  left_inv := by rintro ⟨_, f⟩; cases f <;> rfl
  right_inv := by decide

/-- An explicit encoding of the function symbols of the language of rings by natural numbers.
It is used to Gödel number the sentences of the language of rings. -/
def ringFunctionsEncodable : Encodable (Σ i, Language.ring.Functions i) :=
  .ofEquiv _ ringFunctionsEquivFin

attribute [local instance] ringFunctionsEncodable

variable {L : Language} [Encodable (Σ i, L.Functions i)] [Encodable (Σ i, L.Relations i)]

/-- The Gödel number of an `L`-sentence `φ`: the natural number encoding the list `φ.listEncode`
of symbols of `φ` (see `FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormula.listEncode`). -/
def godelNumber (φ : L.Sentence) : ℕ :=
  Encodable.encode φ.listEncode

/-- An `L`-theory `T` (a set of `L`-sentences) is *decidable* if there is a computable function
`f : ℕ → Bool` which, applied to the Gödel number of any sentence `φ`, returns `true` if and
only if `φ ∈ T`. -/
def IsDecidableTheory (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : ℕ → Bool, Computable f ∧ ∀ φ : L.Sentence, f (godelNumber φ) = true ↔ φ ∈ T

/-- Gödel numbering is injective on sentences. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem godelNumber_injective : Function.Injective (godelNumber (L := L)) := by
  intro φ ψ h
  have := BoundedFormula.listEncode_sigma_injective (Encodable.encode_injective h :
    (⟨0, φ⟩ : Σ n, L.BoundedFormula Empty n).2.listEncode =
      (⟨0, ψ⟩ : Σ n, L.BoundedFormula Empty n).2.listEncode)
  simpa using this

/-- The empty theory is decidable. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem isDecidableTheory_empty : IsDecidableTheory (∅ : L.Theory) :=
  ⟨fun _ => false, Computable.const _, by simp⟩

attribute [local instance] FirstOrder.Ring.compatibleRingOfRing

/--
Is the first-order theory of the field $\mathbb{F}_p((t))$ of formal Laurent series over the prime
field $\mathbb{F}_p = \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ decidable? That is, is there an algorithm which,
given a sentence $\varphi$ in the language of rings $\{+, \cdot, -, 0, 1\}$, decides whether
$\mathbb{F}_p((t)) \models \varphi$?

The prime $p$ is an implicit parameter of the question. The statement asks whether
$\mathrm{Th}(\mathbb{F}_p((t)))$ is decidable for every prime $p$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 12]
theorem decidable.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime →
      IsDecidableTheory (Language.ring.completeTheory (LaurentSeries (ZMod p))) := by
  sorry

end Decidable

items: Read "Laurent series over ℤ_p" as 𝔽_p((t)) = `LaurentSeries (ZMod p)` with `[Fact p.Prime]`, following the decomposition table (ℤ_p((t)) for the p-adic integers is not a field).
Read "field of polynomials over ℂ" as the rational function field ℂ(t) = `RatFunc ℂ`, following the decomposition table (ℂ[t] is not a field).

The language is Mathlib's `Language.ring` = {+, *, -, 0, 1} with no extra constants (in particular no constant for t and no constants for elements of ℂ). Note that for 𝔽_p((t)) the existential theory in this language is decidable (Anscombe–Fehm) while with a constant for t it is open; the full theory is open in both languages, and the table prescribes the pure ring language.

Decidability is formalized as: ∃ computable f : ℕ → Bool such that for every sentence φ, f(⌜φ⌝) = true ↔ φ ∈ Th(K), where ⌜φ⌝ = `Encodable.encode φ.listEncode` uses Mathlib's list encoding of formulas together with an explicit `Encodable` instance on the five ring function symbols (via an equivalence with `Fin 5`). Mathlib has no `Primcodable`/`Encodable` instance for sentences, so `ComputablePred` on sentences could not be used directly; the ℕ → Bool formulation is the standard definition relative to an effective Gödel numbering and is independent of the choice of effective numbering. Injectivity of the numbering is proved as an API lemma.

The prime p is quantified inside the `answer(sorry) ↔ ...` ("is Th(𝔽_p((t))) decidable for every prime p?"), as permitted by the decomposition notes and required by the repository's answer linter (which rejects theorem parameters before `answer(sorry) ↔`). A per-prime variant with p as a parameter would have to disable that linter, so it was not added.

The theory of K is `Language.ring.completeTheory K = {φ | K ⊨ φ}` with the local instance `compatibleRingOfRing`, so `K ⊨ φ` is evaluated with the actual field operations of K (checked by printing the elaborated statement).
AMS tags 3 (mathematical logic) and 12 (field theory and polynomials).

reviewer_notes: Statement issues: (1) 'ℤ_p' must be read as 𝔽_p = ZMod p (Laurent series over the p-adic integers are not a field) — all candidates and the final file do this; p is quantified over all primes after answer(sorry) (positive answer = decidable for every prime), as the table permits and the AnswerLinter requires. (2) 'Field of polynomials over ℂ' can only mean ℂ(t) = RatFunc ℂ; but I believe Th(ℂ(t)) is known undecidable (Duret 1986), with only H10(ℂ(t)) open, so slot ii is omitted rather than shipped with a likely wrong `research open` tag — a human should verify Duret's result; if it is confirmed, the slot could be added as `research solved` with answer(False), or the table should be changed to the existential theory. Modeling of 'decidable theory': Mathlib has no Primcodable instance for formulas (explicit TODO), so the file fixes an explicit Gödel numbering (Encodable.encode ∘ BoundedFormula.listEncode with an explicit Fin 5 encoding of the ring symbols; verified computable by #eval and injective by a proved API lemma) and defines IsDecidableTheory T as the existence of a Mathlib-`Computable` f : ℕ → Bool with f ⌜φ⌝ = true ↔ φ ∈ T. Theory = Language.ring.completeTheory with the structure from compatibleRingOfRing (pure ring language, no constants for t). Generic helpers (godelNumber, IsDecidableTheory) sit in the problem file since only one file could be produced; a maintainer may move them to FormalConjecturesForMathlib. Namespace `Decidable` follows the candidates' problem-name convention (theorem is Decidable.decidable.parts.i); it collides with the core class namespace but causes no conflicts. File builds with `lake --wfail build` (only sorry warning).
